title: Same Speed, New Velocity? Explained Simply | PUC Physics Class 11
description:
Aarav and his friend leave the college gate, both speedometers at 18 km/h. Ten minutes later they are 6 km apart. Same speed, different velocity. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Physics (NCERT Chapter 2, Motion in a Straight Line) we learn exactly how speed and velocity differ.

Two riders run on one road with a live readout and a position-time graph: same speed, velocities +5 and -5 m/s, opposite slopes. We write average speed and average velocity step by step, show link by link why velocity is a vector, compare a round trip side by side, and watch a steady speed on a circle with a velocity arrow that keeps turning. Then a worked example (12 km/h vs 4 km/h), the exam trap, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, JEE Main and NEET students.

In this video:
0:00 Same speed, 6 km apart
0:29 Speed and velocity: what they are
0:54 Live sim: two riders, one road
1:36 Average speed and average velocity
2:14 Why velocity is a vector
2:40 Round trip side by side + pause and think
3:12 Steady speed on a circle
3:49 Worked example: 12 km/h vs 4 km/h
4:22 Exam trap
4:41 Practice question (JEE Main pattern)
5:25 Recap and three questions

Next episode: Average and Instantaneous Velocity. A speedometer shows your speed right now, not your average: how do we find velocity at one instant?
